Cerebrum & Cerebral Cortex

The cerebrum consists of two hemispheres linked by the corpus callosum. The layered cortex (grey matter) overlays white‑matter tracts and supports perception, language, planning, working memory, and executive control. Columnar microcircuits enable parallel distributed processing across areas.

Four Lobes — quick roles

Frontal

Planning, decision‑making, inhibition, working memory, voluntary motor control; speech production (Broca’s area).

Parietal

Multisensory integration, body schema, spatial attention; numerical and symbolic processing.

Temporal

Audition, language comprehension (Wernicke’s), object/face recognition; episodic & semantic memory links.

Occipital

Vision: from orientation/edges (V1) to complex features in extrastriate cortex.

Limbic System

Emotion–memory circuitry integrating hippocampus (episodic encoding/replay), amygdala (salience/affect), cingulate cortex (conflict/motivation), fornix/mammillary bodies (declarative pathways), and nucleus accumbens (reward learning).

Thalamus & Hypothalamus

Thalamus: central relay and attention gateway; contributes to thalamo‑cortical rhythms that scaffold sleep and selective processing.

Hypothalamus: regulates homeostasis (temperature, hunger, circadian rhythm), interfaces with the endocrine system, and shapes motivational states.

Basal Ganglia

Caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, substantia nigra, and subthalamic nucleus implement action selection, habit formation, procedural learning, and reward prediction through dopaminergic signaling (direct/indirect pathways).

Cerebellum

Predictive “forward models” for movement and cognition; error‑driven learning tunes timing, coordination, and sequencing via cortico‑cerebellar loops.

Brainstem

Midbrain (reflexes, dopamine pathways), pons (cerebellar relay, sleep), medulla (autonomic functions). The reticular formation modulates arousal and attention.

Large‑Scale Networks

  • Default Mode Network (DMN): autobiographical memory, mind‑wandering, imagination.
  • Salience Network: flags behaviorally relevant stimuli; toggles between DMN and executive systems.
  • Central Executive Network: working memory, planning, problem solving.
  • Hippocampal–cortical loops: consolidation and replay that integrate episodic traces with neocortical knowledge.

Select – Change – Reconstruct

Phase Neural basis Key structures
Select
(attention & encoding)		 Salience competition; top‑down biasing; thalamo‑cortical rhythms Thalamus, prefrontal & parietal cortex, amygdala
Change
(plasticity & consolidation)		 Synaptic modification, hippocampal replay, cerebellar error learning Hippocampus, basal ganglia, cerebellum
Reconstruct
(recall & imagination)		 Pattern completion and integration with the self‑model Hippocampus, medial PFC, temporal cortex
